name: Socket.IO
solves: Provides bidirectional, event-driven communication between browser clients and servers with automatic transport fallback (WebSocket, HTTP long-polling, WebTransport), reconnection logic, room-based broadcasting, and multiplexing via namespaces.
best_for: Real-time chat applications requiring rooms, presence, and message acknowledgments
Live dashboards and collaborative editing where server pushes updates to specific client groups
Multiplayer browser games needing low-latency bidirectional event-based messaging
Applications behind restrictive corporate proxies where WebSocket may be blocked and transport fallback is essential
Event-driven architectures requiring typed namespaces, middleware pipelines, and structured client-server contracts
skip_when: You only need server-to-client streaming and Server-Sent Events (SSE) would suffice
You need a standards-based WebSocket connection without proprietary protocol overhead for interoperability with non-Socket.IO clients
You are deploying on serverless/edge functions (Vercel, Cloudflare Workers) where persistent connections are not supported
You prefer a fully managed realtime service with guaranteed uptime SLAs and zero infrastructure management
You need MQTT or other IoT-specific protocols for device-to-device communication

hosted_alternative.name: Pusher
hosted_alternative.pricing_summary: Free tier with 200k messages/day and 100 concurrent connections; paid plans from $49/mo scaling with connections and messages
